In the simplest case where 𝑚 = 0, the map Λ is in fact a Banach space isomorphism between Lip𝛼(𝐾) and CH0,𝛼(𝐾). As a result, we can identify 𝛼-fractional 0-charges over 𝐾 with 𝛼-Hölder continuous functions on 𝐾. In this case, it is known that Lip𝛼(𝐾) is the double dual of the little Hölder space, described for example in [28, Chapter 4]. We treat the general case 𝑚 ⩾ 0 by analogy. We define the space of little 𝛼-fractional 𝑚charges ch𝑚,𝛼(𝐾) as the closure in CH𝑚,𝛼(𝐾) of {Λ(𝜔|𝐾) : 𝜔 smooth}, and we establish that F𝑚𝛼(𝐾) ch𝑚,𝛼(𝐾)∗. Thus any bounded sequence in F𝑚𝛼(𝐾) possesses a weakly convergent subsequence, by the Banach-Alaoğlu theorem. Convergence in flat norm is later obtained by adapting the classical deformation theorem to the setting of fractional currents.

- 1.3. Generalized Stokes’ formula. The exterior derivative operator for fractional charges is well-defined as the adjoint of the boundary operator. Specifically, d𝜔 is the 𝛼-fractional (𝑚 + 1)-charge over 𝐾, given by

⟨d𝜔,𝑇⟩ = ⟨𝜔, 𝜕𝑇⟩ (2)

for𝑇 ∈ N𝑚(𝐾). If 𝐾 is convex, this formula extends more generally to 𝛼-fractional currents over 𝐾.

A particular case of this formula is worthy of attention, as it results in a generalized Gauss-Green formula for Hölder vector fields over fractal boundaries. It extends the work of Harrison and Norton [17] (it should be however stressed that formula (2) is purely definitional, contrary to the more constructive Gauss-Green formulas in [17, 16]). Indeed, we can take for 𝑈 a bounded open set with finite (1 − 𝛼)-perimeter (meaning that

𝑈 ∈ 𝑊𝑐1−𝛼,1(R𝑑), or equivalently, ⟦𝑈⟧ is 𝛼-fractional). We shall prove that this condition is weaker than the (𝑑 − 1 + 𝛼)-summability (see [17, §3] or Subsection 3.2) of 𝜕𝑈 that is required in the Gauss-Green formula of Harrison-Norton. In this case, formula (2) applies for 𝑇 = ⟦𝑈⟧ and 𝜔 that is associated to an 𝛼-Hölder continuous (𝑑 − 1)-form.

ours, as they address the casewhere the components 𝑓𝑖 of 𝑓 have different Hölder exponents.

Our contribution is to provide a functional-analytical setting to this construction by showing that 𝑓# is a bounded linear map between spaces of fractional currents. Indeed, in Section 8, we define the pushforward 𝑓#𝑇 of an 𝛼-fractional 𝑚-current 𝑇 by a 𝛾-Hölder continuous map 𝑓 . The construction makes sense as long as 𝑚 + 𝛼 < 𝛾(𝑚 + 1). Under this assumption, we show that 𝑓#𝑇 is 𝛽-fractional, where 𝛽 is given by the equation
